accuracy.evidence: Every number was recomputed: the L-shape (10, 4, 6, 4, 4, 8) sums to 36 cm, equal to its 10 by 8 bounding rectangle; shape 1 (12, 9, ?, ?, 7, 5) has hidden sides 12 − 7 = 5 and 9 − 5 = 4, perimeter 42 cm; shape 2 (4, 3, ?, ?, 11, 8) has hidden sides 11 − 4 = 7 and 8 − 3 = 5, perimeter 38 m; any corner cut of the 10 by 8 rectangle keeps 36 cm while the area is 80 − (10 − x)·y; a 2 cm wide slot of depth d gives 36 + 2d, so 44 cm needs d = 4. Challenge answers checked (9 by 6 corner-cut L = 30 cm; 15 − 9 = 6 m; sides 8, 3, 5, 4, 3, 7 close up and total 30 cm). Definitions match the National Curriculum in England Year 4 and Year 5 statutory wording and the NCETM Year 5 Measures spine.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the errors listed in NCETM's perimeter guidance and Year 5 assessment notes: adding only the marked sides and missing one (Ann, challenge tag missed), counting a side twice (the walk step refuses a second tap and names the slip), adding the pieces instead of subtracting (Gia, step 2 predict option 19 cm, tile feedback, tag add, m4), assuming the two pieces are equal (Ida, option 7 cm, tag copy), confusing perimeter with area (Col, tag area), and 'less area means less perimeter' (Dee, step 3 predict 'It gets smaller', m6, tag smaller), plus counting a slot's depth once (step 4 predict '1 cm', tag once).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab, including flagcolony and flagerode from this run). The prerequisite 462 flagperim walks round rectangles and stretches a 24 cm rectangle; 661 and 507 tile area. This lab is about composite shapes only: tapping the six sides of an L, a missing-side finder that highlights the opposite parallel sides before the learner picks a length, a draggable corner cut that leaves the perimeter fixed while the area changes, and a slot whose depth adds twice to the perimeter.

lab_teaches.evidence: The running sum appears side by side as the learner taps, so the sixth side is discovered rather than told. Tapping a ? side lights up the parallel sides opposite in purple before any choice is offered, so 'pieces add up to the whole opposite side' is seen first and the learner must choose the subtracted value. Dragging the corner to three different places shows three different areas next to an unchanging 36 cm, and the purple new sides make the reason visible. Deepening the slot moves the perimeter in steps of 2 until 44 cm.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 asks how many sides an L has with '4' as the tempting answer; six taps are needed. Step 2 asks for the ? piece with '19 cm' (adding) and '7 cm' (copying) as tempting answers; both are rejected in the lab with the named slip. Step 3 asks what a corner cut does to the perimeter with 'It gets smaller' as the tempting answer, disproved by three cuts at 36 cm. Step 4 asks how much a 1 cm deeper slot adds with '1 cm' as the tempting answer, disproved by the 2 cm jumps.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Each distractor has a tag with its own message: smaller (corner cut swaps two lengths for equal ones), area (that number is length × width in square units), add (the pieces make the whole side, so subtract), copy (the pieces are not equal), once (two walls, so 2 × depth), corner and missed. Lab feedback is equally specific: a repeat tap says the side was already counted; wrong tiles say 'you added' or 'copies another side'; a wrong slot depth says whether it is too short or too long and that each 1 cm changes the perimeter by 2 cm.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py gives the kid text grade 3.4 (limit 6.5) and the adult text grade 8.5 (limit 9.5). Kid sentences are short and concrete with a worked number in each paragraph (12 − 7 = 5 cm, 3 + 3 = 6 cm); 'compound shape' and 'perimeter' are explained on first use; the precise terms composite and rectilinear appear in the key idea and adult text.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph teaches one rule the lab tests (walk round, subtract for gaps, corner cut keeps perimeter, slot adds twice its depth); the adult text gives curriculum references, the five tasks and named mistakes; item hints point to a step or a check rather than repeating the question.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android, light and dark) and 1200 px desktop after moving the shapes down 20 px so the running total never covers the top side's label: all six side labels sit outside their sides in white pills, the corner-cut header was split into 'Perimeter … Area …' and a smaller 'cuts tried' line so it no longer clips at 360 px, the three length tiles are 50 px tall, and the drag handles have 56–60 px hit boxes. Every action also has a full-size button under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, every task completes with Show me, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button ('Side n: 10 cm', 'Find the ? after 9 cm' then one button per length, Cut wider/narrower/deeper/shallower, Slot deeper/shallower, '<name> is right'), and the aria-label is rewritten after each action with the side lengths in order, the running sum, the ? sides, the cut size with perimeter and area, or the slot depth and perimeter.
